page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc7.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores with an x86_64 architecture, utilizing the Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark data places this instance consistently in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1562.49 and a multi-core score of 16538.21. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block bandwidth of 927.07 GB/sec, which drops to 64.29 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and a write bandwidth of 38.96 GB/sec. In application-specific tests, the instance processes 15.27 million Redis SET operations per second and delivers a static web serving throughput of 12.68 GB/sec.

A key tradeoff of the ecs.hfc7.4xlarge is its memory density and lack of local storage. With only 2.0 GB of RAM per core, it is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data processing. This limitation is highlighted in LLM inference benchmarks, where prompt processing for a medium 7B model drops to a weak tier of 23.28 tokens/sec, and 70B models are unsupported. However, the dedicated CPU allocation and 3.3 GHz clock speed make it cost-efficient for compute-bound tasks such as software compilation, text processing, and web serving where high memory-per-core ratios are not required.
